papers.title: For Generalised Algebraic Theories, Two Sorts Are Enough
papers.abstract: Generalised algebraic theories (GATs) allow multiple sorts indexed over each other. Categories have two sorts, objects and morphisms, and the latter are double-indexed over the former. Martin-L\"of type theory has four sorts: contexts, substitutions, types and terms. For example, types are indexed over contexts, and terms are indexed over both contexts and types. In this paper we show that any GAT can be reduced to a GAT involving only two sorts: a first one without dependencies, and another one indexed over the former. We show that a model of the reduced GAT is equivalently given by a pair consisting of a model of the original GAT, which we call the core model, and a "cartesian" morphism from the family of sets induced by this core model. In a type-theoretic metatheory, the initial model of a GAT is called a quotient inductive-inductive type (QIIT). The above characterisation justifies soundness of the reduction, in the sense that the QIIT of the original GAT can be simulated from the QIIT of the reduced GAT, by taking its core model. A particular case of our reduction is the well-known method of reducing mutual inductive types to a single indexed family. Other instances of this reduction can be found in the literature to simulate sophisticated QIITs in Cubical Agda. Indeed, the reduced GAT is simpler than the original GAT in the following aspects: it does not have sort equalities; it does not have interleaved sorts and operations; if the original GAT did not have interleaved sorts and operations, then the reduced GAT won't have operations interleaved between different sorts. Our approach is semantic in that it does not rely on a syntactic description of GATs, but instead, on Uemura's bi-initial characterisation of the category of (finite) GATs in the 2-category of finitely complete categories with a chosen exponentiable morphism.

papers.title: Override and Update in Restriction Categories
papers.abstract: We study the override and update operators on partial functions from the perspective of restriction categories. We propose a definition of override restriction categories, in which both of the operators in question exist. We prove a number of results concerning these operators and their relationship to the structure of the ambient restriction category, as well as relating them to the existing literature on the override and update operators. We provide various examples of override restriction categories and in particular show that every classical restriction category is an override restriction category.

papers.title: Closed layers in tensor-triangular geometry
papers.abstract: In the absence of a theory of closed immersions in tensor-triangular geometry, we propose an alternative approach via quotients of module categories. As an application, we prove invariance of homological residue fields under completion.

papers.title: Pre-Model Structures on the Category of $C_p$-Sets
papers.abstract: It is a folk theorem of Goodwillie that there are exactly 9 model structures on the category of sets, coming from 18 pre-model structures. We investigate model structures and pre-model structures on the category of $G$-sets for a finite group $G$. We outline a strategy for finding all model structures in this category, and partially execute this strategy for the case of $C_p$-sets, where $C_p$ denotes a cyclic group of prime order $p$. In particular, there are exactly 1777 pre-model structures on the category of $C_p$-sets.

papers.title: Hermitian K-theory for stable $\infty$-categories IV: Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt theory
papers.abstract: In analogy with the passage from connective to non-connective algebraic K-theory, Schlichting put forward the Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt spectrum as an approximation to Grothendieck-Witt theory by a functor invariant under idempotent completion. In this paper, we extend his construction to the setting of Poincar\'e $\infty$-categories and characterise the resulting functor by the expected universal property. Our main result places these Karoubi-Grothendieck-Witt-spectra in an exact sequence involving the ultimately decorated L-spectrum and homotopy orbits of non-connective K-theory. This confirms a conjecture of Williams which had remained open even for rings in which $2$ is invertible, and allows us to deduce universal characterisations for ultimately decorated L-theory. We obtain these results by unifying the Bass-Heller-Swan and Ranicki-Shaneson splittings into a general decomposition theorem that yields, in particular, formulas for Grothendieck-Witt groups of Laurent polynomial rings. Finally, we construct multiplicative structures on both versions of our Grothendieck-Witt and L-functors and refine their universal properties to multiplicative ones. Along the way, we show that the original versions are even idempotent with respect to Day convolution.

papers.title: Ostrik's Theorem for Operator Algebras in a Unitary Tensor Category
papers.abstract: We define Hilbert modules for $\mathrm{C^*}$ and $\mathrm{W^*}$ algebra objects in the ind-completion of a unitary tensor category. We then prove an operator algebraic Ostrik's theorem in an ind-category: the 2-category of $\mathrm{C^*}$ or $\mathrm{W^*}$ algebras objects, their modules, and adjointable intertwiners is $\dagger$-equivalent to the 2-categories of $\mathrm{C^*}$ or $\mathrm{W^*}$ module categories.

papers.title: G-radical-square-zero algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first provide necessary and sufficient conditions for a Krull-Schmidt triangulated category with Auslander-Reiten triangles to have square-zero radical. One of these conditions is that the middle term of every Auslander-Reiten triangle is either zero or indecomposable. We then call an artin algebra {\it G-radical-square-zero} if the stable category of Gorenstein-projective modules has square-zero radical. We characterize when a G-radical-square-zero algebra is CM-finite and, in this case, give an additive generator of the stable category. For certain Iwanaga-Gorenstein G-radical-square-zero algebras, we further show that the stable category admits an additive generator consisting of higher syzygies of simple modules.

papers.title: A torsion theoretic interpretation for sheaves of modules and Grothendieck topologies on directed categories
papers.abstract: We prove that every Grothendieck topology induces a hereditary torsion pair in the category of presheaves of modules on a ringed site, and obtain a homological characterization of sheaves of modules: a presheaf of modules is a sheaf of modules if and only if it is saturated with respect to torsion presheaves, or equivalently, it is right perpendicular to torsion presheaves in the sense of Geigle and Lenzing. We also study Grothendieck topologies on directed categories $\mathscr{C}$ satisfying certain finiteness condition, and show that every Grothendieck topology on $\mathscr{C}$ is a subcategory topology if and only if $\mathscr{C}$ is an artinian EI category. Consequently, in this case every sheaf category is equivalent to the presheaf category over a full subcategory of $\mathscr{C}$. Finally, we classify all Grothendieck topologies on a special type of noetherian EI categories, and extend the locally self-injective property of representations of $\mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{VI}$ to representations of their infinite full subcategories. Some potential applications in group representation theory are given at the end of this paper.

papers.title: The Benson--Etingof--Ostrik conjecture for finite tensor categories
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic admits a symmetric tensor functor to a higher Verlinde category. This was conjectured for arbitrary symmetric tensor categories of moderate growth by Benson, Etingof and Ostrik. The proof uses higher Frobenius functors, introduced by the authors in [CF1]. The main effort is directed towards a proof of a conjecture from [CF1] about thick tensor ideals in the representation category of elementary abelian $p$-groups, which implies that the higher Frobenius functors are symmetric monoidal. In fact, we prove a refinement of the latter conjecture that relates tensoring with restricted Steinberg modules to an iterated generalised cohomology of modules of elementary abelian $p$-groups.

papers.title: Stable compatibility for model categories
papers.abstract: By introducing the notion of stable compatibility, we provide a framework in the model category theory which addresses the existence of a stable model structure on the category of modules over a monad. Exact version of such monads have been studied in the setting of triangulated categories, separately as separable monads a la Balmer in tensor triangular geometry and non-separable monads a la Dell'Ambrogio and Sanders in stable homotopy theory. By introducing stable compatibility, we explore their properties together and produce a non-separable monad in Algebraic geometry and more.

papers.title: An Algebraic Abstraction of the Localic Sheafification via the Tripos-to-Topos Construction
papers.abstract: Localic and realizability toposes are two central classes of toposes in categorical logic, both arising from the Hyland, Johnstone and Pitts tripos-to-topos construction. We investigate the common geometric structure underlying these classes by developing an algebraic abstraction of localic presheaves, localic sheafification, and the role of supercompactification in the Comparison Lemma. The resulting framework applies to a broad class of toposes arising from the tripos-to-topos construction, including all $\set$-based triposes. These results establish a common geometric framework encompassing both localic and realizability toposes.
